title: Graceful retirement of vendor model aliases and client adaptor plan
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Summary:
We will retire a small set of legacy vendor model aliases that were used by early customers and 3rd-party integrations. These aliases map to external-vendor-compatible model variants and inject compatibility shims in the serving layer. The long-term plan is to unify model routing through the canonical model alias surface and remove vendor-specific fallbacks to reduce maintenance overhead and accidental performance regressions.

Scope and goals:
- Identify all active vendor model aliases and quantify traffic (by route, client, and region).
- Provide a client-side adaptor library and migration checklist to automatically rewrite alias usage to canonical model ids with feature gates.
- Run a three-stage rollout (observe -> opt-in -> enforcement) with telemetry gates and rollback criteria.
- Preserve backward compatibility for high-value customers with a dedicated opt-in extension period.
- Deliver runbook, FAQ, and SDK patch to minimize client friction.

Out of scope:
- Deprecation of model architecture variants (weights-level changes) is handled in a separate PRD.
- Enterprise contractual changes for Dedicated customers; those customers will be coordinated via Sales/CS separately.
background: Legacy vendor aliases were introduced in 2023 to allow rapid testing of partner models and to support a small set of integrations. Over time these aliases have proliferated and prevented consistent routing, telemetry, and kernel selection optimizations. A small but steady portion of traffic still targets these aliases; without a phased plan we'll continue to suffer complexity tax and unexpected fallbacks that increase latency and cost.
risks: Customer breakage for unmanaged clients if enforcement occurs too quickly
Telemetry blind spots for multi-tenant proxies
Edge cases where alias maps to multiple model variants causing routing ambiguity
success_metrics: >90% of traffic to retired aliases rewritten or using adaptor within 8 weeks of enforcement
No P0 production incidents attributable to alias retirement during rollout window
Latency regression <= 5% for affected routes after migration
acceptance_criteria: Public migration guide published and linked in SDK changelog
Client adaptor library published in NPM/PyPI with tests and usage examples
Rollout plan (observe/opt-in/enforce) scheduled and approved by Product/Eng/SRE
Telemetry dashboards for alias usage, error rates, and latency created and validated
Fallback retention window and enterprise extension policy documented
deliverables: Client adaptor library (JS + Python) and example apps
SDK patch notes and migrations checklist
Customer outreach template and CS handoff doc

implementation_notes:
Implementation will rely on a short-lived compatibility layer in the router that can be toggled per-tenant. ENG-7219 will expose an internal mapping endpoint; adaptor library will rewrite requests client-side and emit explicit telemetry tags 'alias_migrated' and 'alias_fallback'. Canary rollout in eu-west-1, then us-west-2, then global. Enterprise extension flags stored in customer config.

Rollback criteria:
- Alias-related error rate > 2x baseline for 10m and not improving after mitigation steps
- Latency regression > 15% for affected p95 for 3 consecutive windows
If triggered, immediately revert enforcement gate and contact impacted customers via CS.
communication_plan: Phase 1 (Observe): Internal announcement + dashboard link. Phase 2 (Opt-in): Publish migration guide, SDK adaptor release, and email to top 50 customers with sample code. Phase 3 (Enforce): 30-day advance notice to remaining affected customers, Console banner 14 days prior, final enforcement with support on pager for first 72 hours.
customer_outreach: Draft email templates for Opt-in and Enforcement phases
notes_for_eng: Provide a lightweight feature flag in the router to map retired alias to canonical id with reason code. Ensure that logs include original alias, mapped id, and migration_tag for downstream billing reconciliation.
qa_plan:
- Unit tests for adaptor library and router mapping
- Integration tests covering alias->canonical mapping and fallback behavior
- End-to-end smoke in canary region with a synthetic traffic load
- Post-enforcement 7-day monitoring and regression analysis
regulatory_considerations: No new data transfer is introduced by this change; ensure audit logs for route mapping in Private deployments are recorded per customer KMS policies.
